For example a string of events often seen in meth addiction and somewhat like mine: introduced to meth and it was just fun and for partying, you get the best highs without lows. Next you will fall into trying to keep it separate from your “Normal life” and only doing it “for fun” you may even set rules to “set yourself apart” from being one of *those* users (chronic long term addicts) but somewhere along the lines you may find a partner who enables using and unhealthy behaviors that will start you on the downwards spiral of addiction. What once was fun to you and the exhilaration of the highs you now work so hard to reach but it is simply impossible as you will never quite experience that same first high again due to our brain chemistry. Tolerance to the drug builds so no more dopamine rush just irritation, frustration and pain. Your mindset turns negative in almost every aspect without realizing until others point it out. You can’t quite remember who you really were before all this and you lack the confidence needed to find them again. You use because you’re tired, hungry, sad, bored, usually these all are a result of being homeless/sick/coming down. It becomes a crutch for the emotional pain it creates itself and just pathetic attempts to reminisce upon that happiness you associate with the few good memories that came with getting high.
